title: MobiControl Competitor Update — week ending 14 Sep 2026
execSummary: Intune's Week of September 7 release adds two Windows management capabilities; one overlaps a MobiControl differentiator.
Hexnode continues its Windows push (Windows Server management, file deployment) — third consecutive month of Windows-first releases.
No movement from Miradore, 42Gears or Scalefusion this week.

topSignals.headline: Intune expands Windows enrollment-time controls
topSignals.whyItMatters: Closes a gap MobiControl sales currently leads with in regulated-industry deals.

topSignals.headline: Hexnode adds Windows Server management
topSignals.whyItMatters: Signals mid-market UEMs treating servers as endpoints; watch for customer asks.

vendors.summary: Service release 2609 focused on Windows enrollment and compliance.

items.title: Example: Enrollment-time device restrictions
items.whatChanged: Administrators can now block enrollment by device model and OS build at the time of enrollment.
items.soWhatForMobiControl: MobiControl offers this via enrollment rules; the differentiator narrows. Positioning should shift to policy depth and rugged-device coverage.

items.title: Windows Server Management
items.whatChanged: Enroll and manage Windows Servers alongside desktops for patching, remote actions and security policies.
items.soWhatForMobiControl: No direct parity gap for MobiControl's core segments; note as a mid-market trend.

crossPlatformSignals.signal: Jamf Pro 11.32 adds inventory attributes for enrollment type and supervision without MDM queries.
crossPlatformSignals.implication: Vendors are reducing MDM-query reliance for inventory; a pattern MobiControl's Windows agent already avoids.

methodology: Twelve public vendor sources fetched on 14 Sep 2026 and compared against the previous week's snapshots. New feed items, new release pages and changed release-note sections were extracted; the analysis covers only those deltas.
